newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki down for third straight day on rate woes.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki down for third straight day on rate woes.

text.p: Bears were in control in Helsinki on Wednesday for the third consecutive session amid international interest jitters ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting next week, brokers said.
The market soon erased early attempts at higher ground and the HEX index closed 1.34 percent lower at 2,852.84, just inches off its session low.
The FOX portfolio and derivatives benchmark fell through support at 1,000 points to end at 995.4, down 1.6 percent.
Sentiment was weak overall and slightly higher than expected U.S. CPI data late in the session made it worse, brokers said.
Telecoms major Nokia opened up but soon slipped below its U.S. close to end at 308.20 markka, down 2.30 markka, accounting for almost a quarter of thin under 500 million markka volume.
Finland's largest banking group Merita was weak as financial shares were particularly hard hit by debt market weakness, down 1.00 markka at 16.80. The share also went ex a 0.20 markka dividend.
Insurer Pohjola which has gained strongly on a restructuring plan fell 2.00 to 137.00 after it said parts of the reshuffle would be delayed.

Among the few advancing issues, Finnlines rose 3.50 markka to 131.50 after a welcome statement that it would use its options to up its stake in Swedish BTL to 32 percent from 26 percent, brokers said.
Investors were very cautious and activity was expected to remain subdued until the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25.
"The bravest investors may buy, but the rest will wait," said one broker. "Nobody is doing anything on this market -- not buying nor selling," said another.
